clue.text: Might one get into a lather in traffic?

definitions.text: Might one get into a lather in traffic?

blocks.clueFragment: Might one get into a lather in traffic?
blocks.note: surface reading: a driver working themselves into a sweat in a jam
setter's reading: a lather is a mass of soap bubbles, so the vehicle you climb into is one named after bubbles

explanation.surface: A motorist stuck in a jam gets hot and bothered.
explanation.walkthrough: Lather is froth made of bubbles; a bubble car is a tiny domed car of the 1950s and 60s, such as the Isetta.
explanation.definitionFit: The small motor with a rounded glass canopy that you climb into is literally a vehicle named for froth.

clue.text: Indian state brings in half Asia's rice initially

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each word in the phrase before it

blocks.note: the first letter of each of these five words

explanation.surface: An Indian region takes in half of the continent's rice crop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brings in' looks like a container signal, but every word from brings to rice just contributes its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Bihar is a large state in eastern India, on the Ganges plain, bordering Nepal.

clue.text: So Simenon was enabling numberless characters

indicators.note: less means without, and number is the abbreviation N, so that letter is dropped
the word's characters, its letters, are taken loose to be set out in a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written; one of its two Ns goes

explanation.surface: Georges Simenon was enabling characters who had no numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove one N from ENABLING and rearrange EABLING to get BELGIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Georges Simenon, creator of Maigret, was born in Liège, so describing his nationality gives this adjective.

clue.text: Free trip winning the thumbs up? On the contrary!

blocks.clueFragment: Free trip winning the thumbs up
blocks.note: surface reading: a prize holiday earning approval
setter's reading: turn it round, so the hitchhiker's raised thumb wins the free ride

explanation.surface: A free holiday wins everyone's approval.
explanation.walkthrough: Hitchhikers stick a thumb up at the roadside; the free ride they win is a lift, so the cause and effect run the other way from the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A ride given free of charge in somebody's car is a lift, the usual reward for hitchhiking.

clue.text: School of fish out East

indicators.note: out here means on the outside, so the fish wraps around the compass point

blocks.note: a common food fish
compass abbreviation

explanation.surface: A school of fish has gone out to the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School of fish' reads as a shoal, but School alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A coed is a school teaching boys and girls together, short for coeducational.

clue.text: Neptune's beard trimmer?

blocks.note: surface reading: the shaving kit of the bearded sea god
setter's reading: a seashore mollusc whose long shell looks like an old cut-throat blade

explanation.walkthrough: Neptune rules the sea, so his shaver would be found on the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: This long narrow bivalve found on sandy beaches is named for its likeness to a folding cut-throat shaver.

clue.text: Forever sinful there: level zero possible?

blocks.note: surface reading: an eternity spent somewhere
setter's reading: the place of the damned dropping to zero degrees, the freezing point

explanation.surface: The sinful stay down there forever; could the bottom level ever be reached?
explanation.walkthrough: Level zero suggests a ground floor, but it is zero on the thermometer, where water turns to ice.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means never, or for an endless time, since the fiery underworld will never get cold.

clue.text: Head over heels in love, we'd sup with many another

indicators.note: another signals a different version, so the letters gathered are formed into some other word

blocks.note: taken as written
love is zero in tennis scoring, shaped like O
taken as written
D is the Roman numeral for 500, a large number

explanation.surface: Two people head over heels in love dine together, with many others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head over heels in love' is a single idiom on the surface, but the definition stops at heels.
explanation.definitionFit: Head over heels literally means turned over, with the top at the bottom, which is the same as inverted.

clue.text: Where Shirley Valentine worked for the Greek state in a National Trust building

definitions.text: Where Shirley Valentine worked for the Greek

indicators.note: building means constructing, so these letters are put together in a new arrangement
in places the verb inside the other letters

blocks.note: taken as written
standard abbreviation
to aver is to declare or state

explanation.surface: Shirley Valentine's Greek job, apparently in a National Trust property.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust is the British charity that looks after historic houses; 'building' doubles as the noun on the surface and the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: In the film Shirley Valentine, the heroine stays in Greece and works in Costas's seaside eatery, a Greek tavern.

clue.text: Polite cry emanating from one such as Catullus

indicators.note: emanating suggests something flowing out and changing form, so the letters come out in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A courteous shout comes out of a Roman writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Catullus was a Roman writer of short personal verses about love and friendship, a classic example of the type.

clue.text: A right shower!

blocks.note: surface reading: British slang exclaiming at a hopeless bunch of people
setter's reading: a downpour that is a real shower in the weather sense

explanation.walkthrough: In British slang 'a right shower' is a useless, contemptible group; read literally it is a proper fall of water.
explanation.definitionFit: Water falling from clouds in drops is precisely what a meteorological shower consists of.

clue.text: Apprentice pirate following Red Queen, I see

indicators.note: following is the abbreviation f. used in references, standing at the front here

blocks.note: f. is the abbreviation for following
taken as written
Elizabeth Regina
taken as written
said aloud, the word is the name of the letter C

explanation.surface: A trainee buccaneer trails after the Red Queen and says 'I see'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' looks like a position word, but it supplies F, the reference abbreviation as in pp. 10 f.
explanation.definitionFit: In Gilbert and Sullivan's The Pirates of Penzance, Frederic is the young man bound as an apprentice to the pirates.

clue.text: As Fenby to Delius, a servant diverse in uses

indicators.note: diverse means varied, so the letters are varied into another order

blocks.note: taken as written
a manservant
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Fenby served Delius in various ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Eric Fenby took dictation of the blind, paralysed composer Delius's last works, acting as his scribe or secretary.

clue.text: Disdain? That's absurd - is he crazy?

indicators.note: crazy means wild and disordered, so the letters lose their order

blocks.note: taken as written, ignoring the dash

explanation.surface: Someone scorns an idea as ridiculous and wonders if the speaker is mad.
explanation.definitionFit: To disdain something is to dismiss it as unworthy, treating it with scorn and refusing to take it seriously.

clue.text: Steps taken by Mao to achieve extended boundary

blocks.note: extended means lengthy
a march is a border region, as in the Welsh Marches

explanation.surface: Chairman Mao's moves to win a wider frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: March as a frontier is an old word, surviving in the Welsh Marches along the England–Wales border.
explanation.definitionFit: The great retreat of 1934–35 by Mao's Red Army across China was a march, a long series of steps on foot.

clue.text: Delivery vehicles dispelling fear in 3s

indicators.note: dispelling scatters something, so the letters are scattered into a fresh order
in sets the rearranged letters inside the cross-referenced word

blocks.note: the plural of the answer to 3 down
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Vans dispelling fear among lifts.
explanation.walkthrough: Delivery here means deliverance, rescue, not parcels.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflatable boats carried for emergencies deliver shipwrecked people from danger, so they are rescue craft.

clue.text: Tough lawman could stand nothing eccentric

indicators.note: standing a word on end turns it round, so these letters are read the other way

blocks.note: a card is an eccentric, comical person
zero

explanation.surface: A hard-line lawgiver who could not tolerate oddballs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eccentric' looks like an anagram signal, but it is the noun card, an oddball.
explanation.definitionFit: Draco was the Athenian legislator whose laws were so harsh that severe rules are still called draconian.

clue.text: Disapproval shown for tumbling down (second half)

indicators.note: tumbling means falling over and over, so the letters are jumbled
second half keeps only the latter half of the word just named

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
the last two of its four letters

explanation.surface: Displeasure is shown when someone falls down in the second half of a match.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrinkled brow is the facial expression people make to show they are displeased.

clue.text: It describes first word in a letter containing it

indicators.note: the run of words holds the answer within it, so look across their letters

blocks.note: runs from the second letter of word to the first letter of letter

explanation.surface: A word that describes the first word in a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: wORD IN A Letter holds the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: First is a number word showing position in a sequence, which grammarians class as an ordinal number.

clue.text: Auden, a singular talent outside the game

indicators.note: outside means the performer surrounds the poet's initials

blocks.note: a performer who plays alone
the poet W. H. Auden's initials

explanation.surface: Auden was a unique talent who stood outside the literary game.
explanation.walkthrough: Auden is identified only by his initials, as poets often are in crosswords; 'singular talent' is a single performer, not genius.
explanation.definitionFit: Solo whist is a card game derived from whist in which a player may bid to win tricks alone.

clue.text: I'm paid to swallow a few - and I'm not scared

indicators.note: to swallow means to take something in, so the small number goes inside

blocks.note: taken as written
V is the Roman numeral five, a few

explanation.surface: A hired hand happy to gulp down a couple and stay brave.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a phrase that describes a person; impavid is a rare word meaning fearless.
explanation.definitionFit: Impavid comes from Latin impavidus, meaning fearless or undaunted, which is what someone unafraid would say of themselves.

clue.text: Highland route with free entry? Get away! No thanks!

indicators.note: entry puts the word for free at the front, where one comes in
No here means without, so the word for thanks is taken out

blocks.note: to rid is to free
taken as written
British informal thanks

explanation.surface: A free-admission hill walk prompts disbelief and a refusal.
explanation.walkthrough: Ta is British informal for thanks. The Ridgeway is an ancient track along the chalk downs of southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ridgeway is a prehistoric track that follows high chalk ridges, so it is an upland path.

clue.text: Quarrel and turn lights out!

indicators.note: turn means turn round, so the following word is read backwards

blocks.note: taps is the bugle call for lights out in the military

explanation.surface: Have a row and switch the lights off in a huff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lights out' looks like an instruction, but it is the name of the bedtime bugle call.
explanation.definitionFit: A spat is a short petty argument, so it is a minor quarrel.

clue.text: Take one-time opera singer making a comeback...

indicators.note: coming back means going the opposite way, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: R for recipe, Latin for take
taken as written
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A former opera star returns to the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One-time' reads as former but splits into one and time. R comes from the Latin recipe on prescriptions.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenor is the highest standard male voice, and such singers take leading roles in opera.

clue.text: ...as Don Giovanni? That's neglecting his duties, perhaps

indicators.note: neglecting means leaving out, so those letters are dropped
perhaps hints that what remains is only one possible arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
i.e. means that is

explanation.surface: Mozart's Don Giovanni shirks his responsibilities.
explanation.walkthrough: Take IE out of DUTIES and rearrange DUTS. The clue continues from 22: Don Giovanni is an opera rake.
explanation.definitionFit: Don Giovanni is the legendary seducer, and a stud is slang for a man with many lovers.

clue.text: On which tense?

blocks.note: surface reading: a grammar question about verb tenses
setter's reading: the thing you are on when nervous, completing the idiom

explanation.walkthrough: Tense looks like grammar, but it is the adjective: being 'on' this thing means nervous.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'on edge' means anxious and nervy, so this is the word that, after on, means tense.

clue.text: One cooks with aid of vents and North Sea's combustible

indicators.note: combustible things blow up, so the letters are blasted into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
compass abbreviation
taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone cooks using vents and burnable North Sea gas.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests North Sea gas powering a cooker; the words from aid to Sea's are the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: This kitchen appliance cooks food, circulating hot air with an internal fan, so it is something that cooks.

clue.text: Mariner dropped one in fixing sails

indicators.note: fixing means rearranging or repairing, so the letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A sailor lost a crewman while mending the sails.
explanation.walkthrough: Mariner without one I is Marner, so the definition points to George Eliot's Silas Marner, by his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Silas is the forename of Eliot's weaver Marner, whose surname is a seafarer's title with the letter I removed.

clue.text: One can't wait to reach the finishing line

definitions.text: One can't wait to reach the finishing line

blocks.clueFragment: One can't wait to reach the finishing line
blocks.note: surface reading: an eager runner nearing the tape
setter's reading: the last sentence of a book, which an impatient person skips ahead to

explanation.walkthrough: The finishing line is a line of text, the last one in a novel, not the tape at the end of a race.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who peeks at a novel's last page before reading the rest is too impatient to wait for the ending.
